## Introduction

This project explores the stability and cross-dataset agreement of latent
factors derived from sepsis related repeated measure transcriptomic data. To 
do this, we ask the following questions:

1. How much of the variance in each dataset is explained by change over time?
  Or, is the variance completely dominated by between patient factors?

Then, of the different latent factor methods, we ask the following:

1. For those that are stochastic in nature, how stable are the factors across 
  seeds within the same parameter settings?
2. How do the factors discovered at different ranks, and other settings,
  relate to one another?
3. How well do the different bases capture similar patterns across datasets?
4. Is there an 'optimal' method, and within that 'optimal' method are there 
  optimal settings? If so, how stable are these settings?

Since there is no single very large repeated measure dataset, this project
attempts to find general patterns that address these questions by implementing 
different latent factor methods on many different datasets. Currently, 
an analysis of variance is conducted with
[variancePartition](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/variancePartition.html),
and the following latent factor methods are applied to each of 13 configured
datasets:

- [PCA](methods.qmd#pca-one-fit-per-dataset)
- [NMF](methods.qmd#the-methods-and-their-parameters) (only RNA-seq)
- [CoGAPS](methods.qmd#the-methods-and-their-parameters) (only RNA-seq)
- [sPCA](methods.qmd#spca-choosing-the-sparsity)
- [ICA](methods.qmd#ica-icasso-and-kurtosis)
- [WGCNA](methods.qmd#wgcna-one-network-over-all-genes)

The results of each of these analyses is ingested into a SQLite database, and 
displayed with a Shiny app.

## What is in this project?

1. **Calculation** Given [Data](data.qmd) and [Methods](methods.qmd)
  configuration, a [targets](https://books.ropensci.org/targets/) pipeline
  orchestrates the submission and monitoring of all computational steps,
  including the ingestion phase.
2. **Ingestion.** Fits are compared with each other (stability), enriched,
  projected onto the other datasets, described by the repeated-measures model
  and summarized, then written to the database ([Database](database.qmd)).
3. **App.** A Shiny app browses the database ([Launching the app](app.qmd)).

targets re-runs only what a change invalidates: editing one dataset's config
rebuilds that dataset only, editing one method rebuilds that method only
([Running the workflow](workflow.qmd)).
